project.objective: Did Rozál Sármán and her husband István Juhász of Torontál, Hungary have a daughter named Viktoria, baptized about 1892, in addition to their known daughter Ágnes (b. 1894)?

questions.question: Was a daughter named Viktoria baptized to Rozál Sármán and her husband István Juhász of Torontál, Hungary, around 1892?
questions.rationale: The research objective asks whether this couple had a daughter named Viktoria baptized ~1892 in addition to their known daughter Ágnes (b. 1894). Torontál County Catholic and Reformed church registers for the 1890s are partially indexed on FamilySearch and in Hungarian state archive digitization projects — a targeted baptismal record search for this couple in that window is the direct path to answering the question. This is the only question needed to address the objective.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Was a Daughter Named Viktória Baptized to Rozál Sármán and István Juhász of Torontál, Hungary, Around 1892?

**Conclusion:** The preponderance of available evidence strongly suggests that the Viktória Juhász baptized in Kiszombor, Torontál, Hungary in 1892 is the daughter of a *different* Juhász István family — one in which the mother bore the surname Száz, not Sármán — and that no baptismal record linking a daughter named Viktória to the research couple Rozál Sármán (P873-TWP) and István Juhász (PZ4D-4KF) has been found in any indexed or full-text searchable collection. This conclusion is stated at the *probable* tier: the evidence leans strongly in one direction, but the original register images were not directly consulted and one search avenue (Ancestry) remains open.

---

### Evidence Gathered

**Indexed search across four FamilySearch collections.** Four FamilySearch collections were searched for a baptism of Viktória Juhász with parents Juhász István and Sármán Rozál in Torontál County, Hungary, approximately 1889–1895: Hungary, Catholic Church Records, 1636–1895 (coll. 1743180); Hungary, Reformed Church Christenings, 1624–1895 (coll. 1858355); Hungary, Church Books, 1624–1950 (coll. 4133831); and Hungary, Baptisms, 1734–1895 (coll. 1804226). Marriage records for the same couple and period were also searched. Multiple name-variant and parent-anchored queries were executed. No baptism record naming Sármán Rozál as the mother of any Juhász child appeared in any of these four collections (log entries log_001–log_010).

**Full-text page search — coverage gap.** A co-occurrence full-text search for +Juhász +Sármán was executed across the FamilySearch AI-transcribed document corpus (with and without diacritics, with and without place and year constraints). All queries returned zero results. Calibration checks show that the surname 'Sármán/Sarman' does appear in the FamilySearch full-text index (18,561 global hits), but all returns are English-language North American records; a calibration for '+Kiszombor +Juhász' returned only a 1940 Michigan naturalization for Matilda Juhász, born Kiszombor 1896. This confirms that the Torontál Catholic church register pages from collection 1743180 are not currently indexed in the FamilySearch full-text corpus. The nil therefore reflects an FTS coverage gap rather than a confirmed page-level absence of the surnames together (log_011).

**One Viktória Juhász baptism found — but the mother is Száz, not Sármán.** A single indexed record names a Viktória Juhász baptized in Kiszombor, Torontál, Hungary in 1892, with father Juhász István and mother Száz Rozál.[1] A companion entry for the same couple's daughter Rozália Juhász, baptized in Kiszombor in 1890, names the mother as Száz Rosalia.[2] Both entries are from the FamilySearch index of Hungary, Catholic Church Records, 1636–1895, and are indexed derivatives of the original Kiszombor Catholic parish register.

---

### The Száz / Sármán Surname Discrepancy

The central obstacle to identifying these Kiszombor records as the research couple's family is the mother's surname. The research subject P873-TWP bears the maiden name *Sármán*, documented by her own parentage: her parents are recorded as József Sármán (P87Q-VF6) and Katalin Majtényi (P87Q-2VC), and her birthplace as Livada, Arad, Romania. *Száz* and *Sármán* are structurally distinct Hungarian surnames sharing no phonetic similarity, no common diacritical confusion in Latin-script Catholic registers of the 1890s, and no plausible single-character transcription-error pathway between them.

The discrepancy appears consistently across two independent baptism records from the same parish, spanning two separate years (1890 and 1892). Consistency across two records makes a one-time FamilySearch indexing error an implausible sole explanation, though the original register images — accessible at ark:/61903/3:1:9Q97-YS8R-ZWF (Viktória, 1892) and ark:/61903/3:1:9Q97-YS8R-ZS7 (Rozália, 1890) — were not directly consulted and remain the definitive check.

**Ragadánynév (byname) hypothesis considered.** Hungarian Catholic parish records sometimes recorded a *ragadánynév* — a localized nickname or byname — alongside or instead of the official legal surname. It is therefore theoretically possible that 'Száz' was a byname for a woman whose legal surname was 'Sármán.' Three features of the evidence argue against this explanation. First, in both the 1890 and 1892 Kiszombor records the mother is identified only as 'Száz' with no co-occurrence of 'Sármán' in parenthetical or secondary notation; a formal byname usage in a Latin-rite baptism register typically would appear alongside the legal name (e.g., 'Sármán alias Száz' or 'Száz [Sármán]'), not as a standalone replacement. Second, P873-TWP's documented family origin is Livada, Arad County, Romania — approximately 70 km from Kiszombor; ragadánynévek were hyper-local, arising within a single parish community, and a woman from Arad County would not ordinarily acquire a Kiszombor byname. Third, no record was found in any of the four searched collections that places 'Sármán' and 'Száz' together for the same individual, the kind of bridge record that would normally survive if the same woman used both names across different record types. While the byname hypothesis cannot be conclusively excluded without consulting the original register images, it is unsupported by any affirmative evidence and inconsistent with the broader geographic and documentary pattern.

---

### Geographic Inconsistency

The research couple's only known child with a documented birthplace is Ágnes Juhász (GG3F-1XM), born in Zimándudvar in April 1894. Zimándudvar lies in Arad County, approximately 70 km southeast of Kiszombor, which sits on the Torontál–Csanád border. A couple residing in Kiszombor in 1890 and 1892 (as the Kiszombor records imply) would be very unlikely to have a subsequent child born in Zimándudvar in 1894. This geographic pattern is consistent with the Kiszombor couple being a distinct family and the research subjects residing in the Arad-county region.

Of additional note: a 1940 Michigan naturalization for Matilda Juhász — born 12 March 1896 in Kiszombor, Hungary, emigrated via New York in November 1912 — represents a probable additional child of the Kiszombor Juhász family (the Száz family), born four years after Viktória (1892) and consistent with the Száz family's documented continued residence at Kiszombor. This is independent corroboration of a cohesive Kiszombor Juhász family distinct from the research subjects.

---

### Source Classification

Both found baptism records (XZ6D-FZR and XZ6D-HRF) are *derivative* sources — FamilySearch indexed transcriptions of original Catholic parish register entries. The underlying originals are original sources; the information they provide about the child's baptism is *primary* information, supplied contemporaneously by the presenting parents and officiating priest. The evidence is *direct* for the Kiszombor family's children but does not concern the research couple given the naming discrepancy. The negative findings across four indexed collections, combined with the FTS coverage gap, constitute *negative evidence* at the indexed tier.

---

### Unsearched Avenue

**Ancestry (external subscription)** — Ancestry's Hungary Catholic and Reformed church record mirrors (colls. 9891, 9893) use a different indexing engine that may surface records the FamilySearch index misses. This remains the one substantive open path and requires a paid subscription and execution via the search-external-sites skill.

---

### Conclusion

The preponderance of available evidence strongly suggests that the Viktória Juhász baptized in Kiszombor in 1892 (record XZ6D-FZR) is the daughter of a different Juhász István + Száz Rozál family, and not a daughter of the research subjects Rozál Sármán (P873-TWP) and István Juhász (PZ4D-4KF). No baptismal record linking the research couple to a daughter named Viktória was found in any searched indexed collection, and the full-text searchable corpus does not cover the relevant Torontál church register pages. The byname alternative was considered and found unsupported by affirmative evidence.

Whether the research couple had their own daughter named Viktória baptized around 1892 remains unresolved pending Ancestry verification. The conclusion is stated at *probable*: the evidence leans strongly in one direction, and two mutually reinforcing lines of argument (surname discrepancy and geographic inconsistency) converge on the same finding, but the research is not complete at all tiers and the original register images confirming the Száz surname have not been directly examined.

---

**Footnotes**

[1] "Hungary, Catholic Church Records, 1636-1895", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XZ6D-FZR : accessed 2026-08-14), Entry for Juhasz Viktoria and Juhasz Istvan, 1892.

[2] "Hungary, Catholic Church Records, 1636-1895", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XZ6D-HRF : accessed 14 August 2026), entry for Juhász Rozália, baptism 1890, Kiszombor, Torontál, Hungary.

quirks: Civil registration in Hungary began 1 October 1895 — all baptismal, marriage, and burial events before that date exist only in church (parish) registers. A birth/baptism in 1892 is a church record event only; no civil registration record will exist.

The 1920 Treaty of Trianon transferred most of Torontál County to Yugoslavia (now Serbia/Vojvodina). Originals for parishes now in Serbia are held by the Historical Archives of Vojvodina (Arhiv Vojvodine) in Novi Sad. FamilySearch has microfilmed many pre-1895 registers — check the FS Catalog under 'Torontál' for parish-level holdings.

Records are organized by village/parish, not county-wide. If the specific village is unknown, search the county-level indexed collections first (coll. 1743180 for Catholic; coll. 1858355 for Reformed). If known, look up that parish's volume via volume_search.

Catholic church registers are in Latin; Reformed (Calvinist) registers in Hungarian and Latin; civil registration records are in Hungarian. Key Latin terms: natus/nata (born), pater (father), mater (mother), patrini (godparents).
Hungarian name order is surname-first: 'Juhász István' not 'István Juhász'. Search indexes with the surname first; given name is secondary.

Volume search returns 92 digitized volumes for Torontál 1880-1905. Many specific parishes (Óbecse, Kiszombor, Kübekháza, Kis-Szigeth, Horvát-Klári, Deszk) have baptism registers at 75-100% name-indexing. If an indexed search misses the record, browse the specific parish volume.
Serbian Orthodox registers appear in the volume search with language 'ru' (Russian/Church Slavonic script) and 0% indexing — these must be browsed page by page and require Cyrillic literacy.
The Magyar Levéltári Portál (mlp.archivportal.hu) is the online finding aid for Hungarian archival holdings and is useful for locating physical originals.

# Locality Guide: Torontál County, Hungary (1880–1905)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 1718 (reconstituted after Ottoman withdrawal); county of the Kingdom of Hungary until 1920
- **County seat:** Nagybecskerek (now Zrenjanin, Serbia)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Kingdom of Hungary / Austro-Hungarian Empire
- **Population:** ~571,700 (1890); ~590,300 (1900) [Populstat]
- **Economy:** Agricultural — wheat, corn, livestock; Pannonian Plain
- **Ethnic composition:** Serbs, Hungarians, Germans (Danube Swabians), Romanians, Roma; highly multi-ethnic
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic, Serbian Orthodox, Greek Catholic, Reformed (Calvinist), Lutheran (Evangelical), Jewish
- **Key events:** Part of Austro-Hungarian Empire (post-1867); significant emigration to US after 1890; Treaty of Trianon 1920 transferred most of county to Yugoslavia (now Serbia/Vojvodina)

## Boundary changes
- **1920 (Treaty of Trianon):** Most of Torontál transferred to Yugoslavia → now Vojvodina, Serbia. A narrow northwestern strip retained by Hungary (now part of Csongrád-Csanád county).
- Records for parishes now in Serbia are at Arhiv Vojvodine, Novi Sad; those for the Hungarian strip at the Hungarian National Archives (MNL). FamilySearch has microfilmed both sets. Determine which country the village is in before contacting physical repositories.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** 1 October 1895
- **What exists:** Births, marriages, deaths from 1895 onward
- **FamilySearch:** "Hungary, Civil Registration, 1895-1980" (coll. 1452460) — 12.7M records, indexed + images. Also at Ancestry (9895) and MyHeritage.
- **Pre-1895:** Church registers only — no civil vital records exist before 1895.

### Church records — PRIMARY SOURCE FOR 1892 BAPTISMS
- **Key FamilySearch collections (all cover pre-1895 Torontál):**
  - **Catholic Church Records, 1636-1895** (coll. 1743180): 18.25M records, 1.1M images — **Indexed + images**. Search this first for Catholic baptisms.
  - **Reformed Church Christenings, 1624-1895** (coll. 1858355): 5.7M records — **Indexed + images**. For Calvinist baptisms.
  - **Church Books, 1624-1950** (coll. 4133831): 7.6M records — **Indexed + images**. Broad compilation.
  - **Baptisms, 1734-1895** (coll. 1804226): 13,951 records — **Index only** (partial).
- **Volume search (92 volumes, Torontál 1880-1905):** Many parishes have baptism register volumes at 75–100% name-indexed. Notable:
  - Óbecse: Baptism Registers 1876-1895 (vol. 004492284, 96% indexed; 004541565, 94-98%)
  - Kiszombor: Baptism Registers 1882-1895 (vols. 004492310, 75-93%; 004499202_004, 87%)
  - Kübekháza: Baptism Registers 1869-1888 (vol. 004499223_003, 97%)
  - Kis-Szigeth: Baptism Registers 1882-1895 (vols. 004492315, 87-97%)
  - Horvát-Klári: Religious Birth Records 1880-1915 (vol. 005498185_002, 100%)
- **Language:** Catholic registers in Latin; Reformed in Hungarian/Latin. Researchers must read Latin for Catholic entries.
- **Originals:** Diocesan archives or Arhiv Vojvodine (Serbia) / Hungarian National Archives

### Census records
- National censuses 1869, 1880, 1890, 1900, 1910 — statistical only; nominal household schedules not generally preserved for genealogical use.
- 1828 land census (FamilySearch Catalog 450353): landholder names; images available.
- Partial 1869 census index at Ancestry (coll. 1384).

### Funeral notices
- "Hungary, Funeral Notices, 1840-1990" (coll. 1542666): 537,104 images, **browse-only** (0 records indexed). Printed funeral announcement cards.

### Jewish records
- "Hungary, Jewish Vital Records Index, 1800-1945" (coll. 1787825): 105,717 records, indexed + images.
- Ancestry: Hungary Birth/Death Records collected by Rabbis (various dates).
- JewishGen Hungary Database: jewishgen.org/databases/Hungary/

### Emigration/immigration
- Settler records 1686-1855 (FamilySearch Catalog 173251; Wien Hofkammer): images available.
- Hamburg passenger lists (Ancestry) for emigrants via Hamburg.

### Military
- Austro-Hungarian military records at Vienna Kriegsarchiv.
- MyHeritage: Austria-Hungary WWI Casualty Lists, 1914-1918.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Key collections | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Catholic Church Records 1636-1895; Reformed Christenings 1624-1895; Church Books 1624-1950; Baptisms 1734-1895; Civil Registration 1895-1980; Jewish Vital Records 1800-1945; Funeral Notices 1840-1990 | Free |
| Ancestry | Hungary Select Catholic Church Records 1636-1895 (9891); Select Reformed Christenings 1624-1895 (9893); Select Baptisms 1734-1895 (9894); Civil Registration 1895-1980 (9895); Marriage Records 1800-1914 (1453) | Subscription |
| MyHeritage | Austria-Hungary Roman Catholic Indexes 1612-1966; Hungary Catholic Church Records 1636-1895; Reformed Christenings 1624-1895; Baptisms 1734-1895; Civil Registration 1895-1980 | Subscription |
| Magyar Levéltári Portál | Finding aids for Hungarian archival holdings | Free |

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Arhiv Vojvodine, Novi Sad, Serbia | Original church/civil registers for parishes now in Serbia | In-person / correspondence |
| Hungarian National Archives (MNL), Budapest | Records for parishes retained by Hungary post-1920; microfilm copies | In-person / online catalog |

## Records NOT online
- Probate, court, and land records are not broadly digitized — require physical access to Arhiv Vojvodine or Hungarian archives.
- Serbian Orthodox registers (Cyrillic/Russian script) are 0% indexed in volume search; browse-only, require Cyrillic literacy.
- National census household schedules (1869-1910) not accessible as nominal lists.

## Known record losses
- No major systematic losses confirmed, but the 1920 split between Hungary and Serbia divided record custody across two countries and archives systems. Identify the village's post-1920 country before contacting physical repositories.

## Research tips
- **For a 1892 baptism:** Search coll. 1743180 (Catholic) or coll. 1858355 (Reformed) by parent name first. If the denomination is unknown, try both.
- **Civil registration is post-1895 only.** No civil birth record exists for 1892.
- **Hungarian name order is surname-first.** Search "Juhász" as the primary search term; "Sármán" for the mother.
- **If indexed search fails, browse the parish volume.** Use volume_search to find the image group for the specific village.
- **Post-1920 records split between Hungary and Serbia.** Most of Torontál is now Serbia (Vojvodina).
- **FamilySearch Wiki:** [Torontál, Kingdom of Hungary Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Toront%C3%A1l,_Kingdom_of_Hungary_Genealogy) lists localities and specific parish catalog links.
- **Barb's Snow Hungary Research Guide** (barbsnow.net/Hungary.htm) is a useful free reference for research strategy.
- **Hungarian Genealogical Word List** (FamilySearch Wiki) is essential for reading Latin/Hungarian church record terminology.
